newsitem.title: PANAMA: Guatemala concerned about new U.S. immigration law.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala concerned about new U.S. immigration law.

text.p: Guatemalan Foreign Minister Eduardo Stein expressed concern on Thursday about the consequences of a tough new U.S. immigration law for up to 65,000 Guatemalans living in the United States.

"If the 60,000 to 65,000 people there returned at once it would be a true catastrophe," he told reporters at a regional foreign ministers' meeting here. "We received information from U.S. authorities that there wouldn't be massive deportations, but deportations have already begun to occur."

U.S. Attorney General Janet Reno said on Thursday the new immigration law now in effect would lead to more deportations but not massive deportations. But Stein said Guatemala was already confronted with the task of absorbing returnees, demobilized soldiers and former leftist guerrillas.

"At this moment, Guatemala is not only facing the return of more than 5,000 refugees living in camps in Mexico, but also the demobilization of soldiers and ex-guerrillas. We have our hands full of close to 19,000 from these three groups," he said.
